Subject: Next steps from today's residency discussion

Hi Elena — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick summary and a few clarifying asks so we can draft an ops-safe runbook for Medisys: 

Summary
- Primary ask: keep all customer PII and raw request logs in the EU (EU-West preferred).
- Secondary: warm-standby / failover to US region for DR with strict controls.
- Retention: security team mentioned long-term retention requirements (you said ~7 years).

Clarifying questions (so our ops + legal teams can scope):
1) PII definition: please confirm the data classes you consider PII for this project (e.g., name, email, medical identifiers, free-text submissions). Do you require automatic redaction at ingestion or just encryption/segregation?
2) Logs & telemetry: do audit logs (API request/response metadata) need to remain in-region at all times, or can we ship redacted telemetry to a central analytics account?
3) Cross-region snapshots: is replication to US for offsite backups acceptable if snapshots are encrypted with a customer-managed key and access is tightly restricted?
4) KMS: do you require a dedicated KMS key per environment/customer or is dedicated keys per-account sufficient?
5) RTO/RPO expectations for failover (target numbers help us size reserved capacity).

What we'll produce for you next
- Draft residency runbook that includes: pinning config, failover playbook, snapshot encryption flow, logging retention and access controls.
- Proposed canary plan (10% traffic for 2 weeks during business hours) to validate cross-region failover behavior.
- Shorter SOC2/infosec pack with redacted artifacts you can share with your procurement team.

Attachments: call-recording-20271207.mp3 (audio), residency-questionnaire.xlsx

Next steps
- Can you confirm the PII classes and whether ingestion redaction is required?
- If OK, we will send the draft runbook by EOD tomorrow and propose a 30-minute follow-up to review technical constraints (availability: Thurs 11–1pm CET).

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marcus — thanks for the summary and the clear next steps. A few priority clarifications from our side: 

- PII classes: name, email, national ID, medical record numbers, and any free-text clinical notes we store are considered PII.
- Ingestion: we'd prefer automatic redaction for specific fields (IDs), while free-text may be retained but flagged and encrypted.
- Retention: regulatory requirement for logs and primary records: 7 years. For performance logs, 90 days hot / 7 years cold is fine.
- Backups: replication to the US is permissible for DR provided that snapshots are encrypted with our CMK and access is audit-restricted.
- KMS: we expect a dedicated customer-managed key (CMK) scoped to Medisys environments.

We'll need your SOC2 report (redacted) and a short technical runbook to present to procurement/security. Can we do a follow-up call Friday at 10am CET? Michael (security lead) will join.

Best,

Marcus / Grace — forwarding a quick engineering-read of what we can commit to and where we need explicit approvals. Quoted reply from me below.

--- forwarded ---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-07T12:30:00-08:00
To: marcus@redwood.com
Subject: Proposed technical approach (summary)

Short version: we can implement your asks with the following constraints and recommended guardrails: 

1) Pinning & failover
- Primary: EU-West (Frankfurt) placement for pinned datasets and runtime.
- Warm standby: us-west (oregon) with automated traffic routing policy. Failover will be policy-driven (latency threshold or explicit ops trigger).
- Impact: cold latencies and failover traffic will see a 40–60ms increase for token round-trips in DR mode; we should surface that in the runbook.

2) Snapshots & backups
- Snapshots may be replicated to US for DR if they are encrypted with the customer's CMK and stored in a separate, audited bucket.
- We'll add an ops approval gate for exporting any snapshot out of EU.

3) Logs & telemetry
- Audit logs and full request payloads will be stored in EU buckets by default.
- Redacted telemetry can be optionally shipped to central analytics; requires explicit customer consent and a signed DPA addendum.

4) KV cache & inference state
- KV caches (model context) are sticky to the serving region and are not cross-region replicated to avoid leakage. In a failover we rebuild warm caches using last-known prefixes and replay heuristics.

5) KMS
- Support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-key). For DR replication to US we will encrypt snapshots with the CMK prior to export; key policy controls must be provided by the customer.

6) Retention
- Hot tokens/metrics: configurable to 90 days.
- Cold archives: configurable to 7 years in immutable, access-controlled storage.

Actionables I'm proposing:
- Draft runbook (attached): residency-runbook-draft.md
- KMS flow diagram: kms-keyflow-diagram.png
- Ops approval checklist and export gate for any cross-border snapshot movement.
- Recommend canary: 10% traffic for 2 weeks, business hours only.

Risks to flag for customer: slight latency penalty in DR, higher egress/replication costs, and longer restore windows if archives are on cold storage.

Ben
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
